input: Repaint and seal the garden fence before rain

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The total length, height, and material of the fence determines how much paint and sealant is needed, how many coats are required, and how long the job will take.
Knowing exactly when rain is forecast sets the hard deadline and determines whether the job must be done in one session or can be split across days.
The current condition of the fence — peeling paint, bare wood, rot, moss — affects how much prep work (sanding, cleaning, priming) is needed before painting can begin.
Whether the user is working alone or has helpers directly impacts how the work is divided and how realistic the timeline is.
The choice of paint colour and finish type (matte, gloss, wood stain, solid paint) shapes which products to buy and how the end result should look.
Knowing which tools and products the user already owns (brushes, rollers, paint, sealant) determines what needs to be purchased and whether a hardware run is the first action.
Understanding whether the priority is a quick protective coat or a high-quality long-lasting finish determines how many preparation and painting steps are truly necessary.

gold.taskTitle: Repaint and seal the garden fence before rain
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to repaint and seal their garden fence, completing the job before rain arrives.

questions.title: How long and tall is the fence to paint?
questions.description: Establish the total surface area of the fence — its length, height, and material — to estimate paint quantities and time needed.

questions.title: How many days until rain is forecast?
questions.description: Pin down the hard deadline so the plan can be structured around realistic drying and curing windows.

questions.title: What condition is the fence currently in?
questions.description: Determine how much prep work is needed — e.g. peeling paint, bare or rotting wood, moss or dirt — before any painting can begin.

questions.title: Will you be working alone or with helpers?
questions.description: Clarify whether extra people are available, which affects how the workload is split and whether the deadline is achievable.

questions.title: What colour and finish are you going for?
questions.description: Identify the target look — e.g. a natural wood stain, solid colour, gloss or matte finish — to guide product selection.

questions.title: What tools and materials do you already have?
questions.description: Find out which supplies are already on hand — brushes, rollers, paint, sealant, sandpaper — to determine what still needs to be bought.

questions.title: Is this a quick coat or a long-lasting quality finish?
questions.description: Understand whether the priority is speed and basic protection or a thorough, durable result, which determines how many prep and coating steps are required.
